newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money steady, long-term gilts in demand.
newsitem.headline: India call money steady, long-term gilts in demand.

text.p: Indian call money ended Friday at 5.75-6.0 percent in steady, range-bound trade, dealers said.
"Most of the day's trade was around 5.75-6.0 percent," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Trade was range-bound after the opening quotes of 6.0-6.5 percent."
Dealers said funds supply and demand were evenly matched through the day and there were no market-moving factors to give a push to rates either way.

Traded volumes in government securities jumped up sharply, following Thursday's auction, dealers said. They said volumes went up to 3.79 billion rupees at the National Stock Exchange from Thursday's 1.54 billion.
"The security auctioned yesterday was much in demand and was traded at a premium right from the start of trade," said a dealer.
The Reserve Bank of India auctioned 10 billion rupees of 10-year government of India securities on Thursday at a yield of 13.65 percent against earlier issues of 13.85 percent.

"The yield curve underwent an adjustment today reacting to yesterday's auction result," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Prices of medium and long-dated securities went up as there was good demand."

The 13.85 percent 2006 government of India stock traded on friday at 101.86 rupees against its last traded 101.75, the 14. percent 2005 at 103 rupees against 102.82. Dealers said the new security auctioned on Thursday traded at 32 paise above its issue price of 100 rupees.
Deaelrs said there were no trades in commercial paper or certificates of deposit.
